purpose: How Word continues one list across w:num instances of the same w:abstractNum, and when an instance's w:startOverride restarts it (#1243).
procedure: Minimal packages (content types, package and document rels, document.xml, numbering.xml, styles.xml) were opened in Word and each paragraph's `list string of list format` was read through AppleScript; the same packages were converted to PDF with headless LibreOffice and read with `pdftotext -layout`. Paragraph text names the w:num and w:ilvl it uses (e.g. "p3 n4L1").
finding: Word keeps ONE running counter set per w:abstractNum; every w:num over it continues that sequence, at every level. An instance's w:lvlOverride/w:startOverride restarts the shared level at the override value the first time a paragraph of that instance is numbered ON THAT LEVEL, and never again (b, c, c2, e, g, t7; d4 and t3: first use on another level does not trigger it). When a paragraph's level use restarts deeper levels (default or w:lvlRestart threshold), each restarted level resumes at the start value of THAT paragraph's instance, so an override instance re-applies its override on every restart it causes (r3, r4, t1; d2 p8: a plain instance's restart uses the abstract start). w:lvlRestart 0 levels keep counting across instances (d3, t9). LibreOffice 26.2 agrees on sharing and on first-use restarts, but restarts deeper levels at the abstract start (r4, t1 differ) and ignores w:lvlRestart (d3, t9 differ); safe-docx follows Word. Not yet followed (separate defect): Word renders a skipped or never-used ancestor level at its start value and counts it as used (r2, r5), where safe-docx renders 0.
